before: 母亲日夜守在病床前，自己却瘦了一大圈。
after: 母亲日夜守在病床前，人都瘦了一大圈。
why: “自己却瘦了”: 却 sets up a contrast that is not there; “人都瘦了一大圈” is the idiomatic way to say someone visibly lost weight from strain.

before: Mother kept watch by the sickbed day and night and lost a lot of weight herself.
after: Mother kept watch by the sickbed day and night and grew visibly thinner.
why: Matches the revised sentence.

before: I checked my bank card and found only two hundred yuan left in the balance.
after: I checked my bank card and found the balance was down to just two hundred yuan.
why: Smoother, more faithful English.

before: This soccer match was given live commentary by a well-known sports commentator.
after: A well-known sports commentator provided live commentary for this soccer match.
why: Original English passive was awkward.

before: 我把空调设置了定时，两个小时以后会自动关掉。
after: 我给空调设了定时，两个小时以后它会自动关掉。
why: “把空调设置了定时” is an awkward 把-construction; “给空调设了定时” is what people say.

before: 妈妈每天早上给孩子冲一杯奶粉。
after: 妈妈每天早上给孩子冲一瓶奶粉。
why: Infant formula is made up in a bottle (瓶), not a cup; matches the "formula" gloss.

before: Every morning, Mom makes the child a cup of formula.
after: Every morning, Mom makes the baby a bottle of formula.
why: Matches the revised sentence.

before: 自行车的轮子扎了个钉子，没气了。
after: 这辆玩具车少了一个轮子，跑不起来了。
why: A nail punctures the tyre (车胎), not the 轮子; “轮子扎了个钉子” is unidiomatic.

before: The bike wheel picked up a nail and went flat.
after: This toy car is missing a wheel and won't run.
why: Matches the revised sentence.

before: 随着互联网的普及，很多新兴职业出现了，比如网络主播。
after: 随着互联网的普及，出现了很多新兴职业，比如网络主播。
why: Indefinite new subject is introduced with existential word order (出现了很多…), not “很多…出现了”.

before: 这座体育馆规模宏大，可以容纳十万名观众。
after: 这座体育场规模宏大，可以容纳十万名观众。
why: 体育馆 is an indoor gym/arena that cannot seat 100,000; a stadium is 体育场 (the English already said stadium).

before: 下了一夜雪，院子里的梅花开得更红了。
after: 下了一夜雪，院子里的梅花在白雪的映衬下显得更红了。
why: Snow does not make the blossoms bloom redder; they look redder against the snow.

before: After a night of snow, the plum blossoms in the courtyard looked even redder.
after: After a night of snow, the plum blossoms in the courtyard looked even redder against the white.
why: Matches the revised sentence.

before: 这节课的难点是如何区分这两个语法。
after: 这节课的难点是如何区分这两个语法点。
why: “两个语法” is ungrammatical; individual grammar items are 语法点.

before: Now that I'm working, I have to cover all my own living costs and can't rely on my parents anymore.
after: Now that I'm working, I have to provide my own food, clothing, housing and transport and can't rely on my parents anymore.
why: "Living costs" lost the literal meaning of the word being tested.

before: 这些电影实行分级制度，有些不适合儿童观看。
after: 很多国家对电影实行分级制度，有些电影不适合儿童观看。
why: “这些电影实行分级制度” has films as the agent of a policy; a country or authority 实行 a rating system.

before: These films are subject to a rating system, and some aren't suitable for children.
after: Many countries have a rating system for films, and some films aren't suitable for children.
why: Matches the revised sentence.

before: 上海港口每天都有大量货船进出。
after: 上海港是世界上最繁忙的港口之一，每天都有大量货船进出。
why: “上海港口” is not the standard name (上海港); rewritten so 港口 is used as a common noun.

before: Large numbers of cargo ships come in and out of the port of Shanghai every day.
after: The port of Shanghai is one of the busiest in the world, with large numbers of cargo ships coming and going every day.
why: Matches the revised sentence.

before: This year's number of applicants set a record high over all previous years.
after: This year's number of applicants was the highest of any year on record.
why: Original English ("a record high over all previous years") was clumsy.

before: mencuci muka dan menggosok gigi, bersiap-siap
after: mencuci muka dan menggosok gigi
why: "bersiap-siap" (to get ready) is not a meaning of 洗漱.

before: 据统计，野外现存的大熊猫约有一千八百多只。
after: 据统计，野外现存的大熊猫有一千八百多只。
why: 约 together with 多 is redundant (“约有一千八百多只”).

before: According to statistics, there are about 1,800 giant pandas left in the wild.
after: According to statistics, there are just over 1,800 giant pandas left in the wild.
why: Matches the revised sentence.
